findings.title: deleteCache throws a plain Error instead of TRPCError
findings.body: When the credential is not found or does not belong to the caller, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC converts unknown errors into `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (HTTP 500) and reports them to error logging/monitoring as server faults, instead of a 404/403. Use `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" | "FORBIDDEN", message: ... })` so the client gets a correct status and the condition is not reported as a server crash. The UI currently only shows a generic toast, so the mis-typed error also hides the real cause from the user.

findings.title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, so expired cache rows are shown as current
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` aggregates `MAX(updatedAt)` over all `CalendarCache` rows for a credential with no `expiresAt` filter. Rows stay in the table after expiry (expiry is enforced at read time via `expiresAt: { gte: now }` in `getCachedAvailability`), so the UI will display a "Last updated" timestamp and a "Delete cached data" action for credentials whose cache is expired and no longer served. The displayed status is therefore misleading. Filter by `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` (or surface expiry explicitly).

findings.title: Cache status query bypasses the calendar-cache feature gate
findings.body: The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly rather than going through `CalendarCache.init(...)`, which is the factory that returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the calendar-cache feature is disabled. As a result, users/teams without the `calendar-cache` feature enabled will still get cache status and the "Delete cached data" action in the UI, and every `connectedCalendars` request pays an extra `groupBy` query even when the feature is off.

findings.title: deleteCache success does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
findings.body: The `deleteCache` mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop, while the disconnect mutation explicitly invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in `onSettled`. In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` the `onSuccess` prop is wired to `props.onChanged`, which is optional and undefined on the installed-apps page; the `connectedCalendars` query is also configured with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. Consequently, after deleting the cache the dropdown keeps showing the old "Last updated" timestamp and the delete action until a full reload. Invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in the mutation's `onSettled`/`onSuccess`.

findings.title: Cache timestamp hardcoded to en-US locale and browser timezone
findings.body: The timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` regardless of the user's locale (available via `useLocale()`) or the user's configured timezone/time format. Non-English users will see a US-formatted date inside an otherwise localized string, and the time is rendered in the browser timezone which may differ from the profile timezone used elsewhere in the app.

findings.title: updateMany with empty data relies on implicit @updatedAt and writes on every cache refresh
findings.body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is called at the end of every `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` run (including each Google webhook delivery and cron refresh). It passes an empty `data` object and depends entirely on Prisma implicitly adding `updatedAt` to the SET clause; if that behaviour changes or the field is not `@updatedAt`, the call becomes a no-op UPDATE on every selected calendar row for the credential with no visible error. It also performs an extra write over all rows of the credential on a hot path, and per the PR description the resulting `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not consumed anywhere in the UI (the UI uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache`). Either set the timestamp explicitly (`{ updatedAt: new Date() }`) or drop the call.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId typed with SelectedCalendarUpdateInput instead of the updateMany input type
findings.body: `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany` accepts `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`, but the method signature declares `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`, which additionally permits nested relation operations (`user: { connect: ... }`, etc.). Such payloads type-check at compile time but fail at runtime when passed to `updateMany`. Narrow the parameter type to `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId that the function never uses
findings.body: `UserWithCalendars` was widened so `allSelectedCalendars`/`userLevelSelectedCalendars` must include `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`, but nothing in this file (or in the new cache-status code, which reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt`) consumes those fields. This is an exported type used by other callers (platform libraries / API v2 / other handlers) that build the user object with only `externalId | integration | eventTypeId`; those call sites now fail to type-check and require a matching `select` change. Either revert the widening or update all construction sites.

findings.title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` without declaring tsx as a dependency
findings.body: `dev:cron` now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not in `dependencies`/`devDependencies` (while the now-unused `ts-node` remains). `npx` will silently download an arbitrary latest version of `tsx` from the network on each developer machine/CI run, which is non-deterministic and fails in offline/locked-down environments. Add `tsx` as a devDependency and invoke it via the local binary.

findings.title: `sed -i ''` is macOS-only and breaks on Linux
findings.body: The in-place edit uses BSD/macOS syntax `sed -i '' -E ...`. With GNU sed (Linux, CI containers) `-i ''` is parsed as an empty suffix argument followed by the empty string being treated as the script/file, so the command errors out or edits the wrong file, leaving `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` unchanged while the script still prints the success message. Use a portable approach (e.g. write to a temp file and move it, or branch on `uname`).

findings.title: Migration warning comment contradicts the SQL it documents
findings.body: The auto-generated warning block states the column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the SQL actually adds `updatedAt` with `DEFAULT NOW()`, which is safe for non-empty tables. Leaving the stale warning in place is misleading for anyone reviewing or replaying migrations; remove or correct it.

findings.title: No tests for the new cache deletion authorization or cache-status mapping
findings.body: The PR adds a destructive mutation (`deleteCache`) whose only protection is an ownership check on `Credential.userId`, plus a new repository aggregation (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`) and the credential→cache mapping in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`. None of these have unit tests: there is no test asserting that another user's credentialId is rejected, that cache rows of other credentials are not deleted, or that the `credentialId → updatedAt` map is built correctly (including credentials without cache). Given the authorization-sensitive and data-deleting nature of the handler, tests should accompany it.
